Create a file named case_120.inp in the working directory containing the exact input deck text provided between the inp code fences, preserving all whitespace, blank lines, and numerical values exactly as given.
Run CalculiX on the input file by executing the command ccx -i case_120 in the working directory. If that invocation fails due to argument parsing, retry with ccx case_120.
Capture the CalculiX version string by running ccx -v (or ccx --version if -v is not recognized) and record the first line of output.
After the solver finishes, open the file case_120.sta in the working directory and search for the string "JOB COMPLETED" to determine success. If that string is present, the run succeeded; if the file is missing or does not contain that string, the run failed.
If the run failed, read the end of case_120.sta and any case_120.dat or case_120.msg files to capture the error message and note which file indicated the failure.
Write a file named results.json in the working directory as a single JSON object with the following fields: solver set to "calculix", case_id set to "case_120", status set to "success" if JOB COMPLETED was found or "error" otherwise, ccx_version set to the version string obtained from ccx -v, artifacts set to an empty list, and notes set to a string that records the exact ccx command that was used (e.g., "ccx -i case_120"), and if the run failed, also includes the error message text and the filename that indicated the failure.
Do not modify any values in the input deck. Do not add or remove any keywords, nodes, elements, boundary conditions, material definitions, or transform definitions.
